question: A group of scientists is conducting an experiment on the human cells involved in the immune response. They genetically modify B cells so they do not express the cluster of differentiation 21 (CD21) on their cell surfaces. The pathogenesis of which of the following organisms would most likely be affected by this genetic modification?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "B cells modified to lack CD21" -> "reduced ability to bind to EBV" -> "impaired immune response to EBV" -> 85%
CHAIN: "B cells modified to lack CD21" -> "no significant effect on measles virus" -> "measles primarily targets T cells" -> 70%
CHAIN: "B cells modified to lack CD21" -> "no direct effect on HIV pathogenesis" -> "HIV primarily targets CD4+ T cells" -> 60%
CHAIN: "B cells modified to lack CD21" -> "no significant effect on HPV" -> "HPV primarily affects epithelial cells" -> 65%
CHAIN: "B cells modified to lack CD21" -> "reduced immune response to EBV" -> "EBV relies on CD21 for entry into B cells" -> 90%
analysis: CD21 is a receptor that plays a crucial role in the immune response, particularly in the activation of B cells and their ability to respond to certain pathogens. Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) specifically uses CD21 as a receptor to enter B cells. Therefore, genetically modifying B cells to not express CD21 would significantly impair the immune response to EBV, affecting its pathogenesis.
